newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A change of wording so that sovereign power "belongs to" and not "comes from" the people could undermine the political reform process. Anand Panyarachun, chairman of the Constitution Scrutiny Committee, says the change is not worth it after his panel is defeated in a vote on whether the draft should maintain the original wording that power originates from the public in Article 3. (BANGKOK POST)

- The one-MP Palang Dharma Party (PDP) is on the brink of breaking up, with most of its Bangkok assemblymen and city councillors threatening to bolt the party en masse to force party leader Chaiwat Sinsuwong to step down. A PDP source says that 12 of 17 PDP assemblymen and 95 of the PDP's 135 district councillors have agreed to quit as party members on July 15 if Chaiwat refuses to step down by this Saturday to pave the way for MP Sudarat Keyuraphan. (THE NATION)

- Thailand is expected to propose the setting up of a task force against drugs with its five neighbours in the Mekong region when it hosts a ministerial meeting on regional cooperation in drug control in Bangkok this week. Thailand and the United Nations International Drug Control Programme are hosting the second ministerial meeting for regional cooperation in drug control in the Mekong region on July 9-11. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Government will let the prices of fuel rise and fall according to real market supply and demand conditions without subsidising sellers. An official says the 13 billion baht Oil Fund will not be utilised since intervention and subsidies are not appropriate measures to apply and will not provide a long-term solution to the problem. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Almost 300 billion baht has been overspent on infrastructure and basic industry in the past three years, causing an oversupply and stalling new listings on the stock exchange. The Board of Investment has encouraged too much funding of basic infrastructure during the period. (BANGKOK POST)
